title: Bible Guide
paragraph: PROPHET IN ISRAEL IN THE DAYS OF AHAB AND AHAZIAH · TWO KINGDOMS

blocks.text: PROPHET IN ISRAEL IN THE DAYS OF AHAB AND AHAZIAH · TWO KINGDOMS
Elijah. The Tishbite who shut the heaven, called fire on Carmel and went up by a whirlwind.
Ahab · Ahaziah of Israel · Jehoram of Judah · Jehu · Hazael
“As the LORD God of Israel liveth, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word.”

Again and again “the word of the LORD came” to him with his next step: to hide by the brook Cherith, to go to Zarephath, to show himself to Ahab in the third year, to meet Ahab in Naboth's vineyard, and that the evil was put off to Ahab's son's days. 1 Kings 17:2–3 1 Kings 17:8–9 1 Kings 18:1 1 Kings 21:17–19 1 Kings 21:28–29

An angel woke him twice under the juniper tree with food for the journey; later “the angel of the LORD” sent him to meet Ahaziah's messengers and told him to go down with the third captain. 1 Kings 19:5–7 2 Kings 1:3 2 Kings 1:15

At Horeb the LORD passed by in a great wind, an earthquake and a fire, “but the LORD was not in” them; after the fire came “a still small voice”, and a voice asked him, “What doest thou here, Elijah?” 1 Kings 19:9–13

He prayed and the text records the answers: the widow's son revived, and the fire of the LORD fell on Carmel. James says he prayed that it might not rain, and prayed again for rain. 1 Kings 17:20–22 1 Kings 18:36–38 James 5:17–18
“The hand of the LORD was on Elijah” when he girded up his loins and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel. 1 Kings 18:46
From the textEvery word of his in Kings is spoken. The one written word is in Chronicles: “a writing” to Jehoram of Judah. 2 Chronicles 21:12
“I have found thee: because thou hast sold thyself to work evil in the sight of the LORD.”
“therefore thou shalt not come down off that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die.”
“And there came a writing to him from Elijah the prophet”
“for the LORD hath done that which he spake by his servant Elijah.”
The word in its main themes
The LORD, not Baal, is God
“How long halt ye between two opinions? if the LORD be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him.”
“The LORD, he is the God; the LORD, he is the God.”
Rain and drought at the LORD's word
“there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word.”
Is there not a God in Israel?
“Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that ye go to enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron?”
Naboth's blood and the house of Ahab
“Hast thou killed, and also taken possession?”
“In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine.”
“Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him.”
Judah judged by the ways of its fathers
“And thou shalt have great sickness by disease of thy bowels, until thy bowels fall out by reason of the sickness day by day.”
To whom the word was spoken
“The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the LORD sendeth rain upon the earth.”
“go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah is here.”
“I have not troubled Israel; but thou, and thy father’s house, in that ye have forsaken the commandments of the LORD, and thou hast followed Baalim.”
“How long halt ye between two opinions?”
“Cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth, and must be awaked.”
“Get thee up, eat and drink; for there is a sound of abundance of rain.”
“Thou hast asked a hard thing: nevertheless, if thou see me when I am taken from thee, it shall be so unto thee; but if not, it shall not be so.”
“Behold, I will bring evil upon thee, and will take away thy posterity”
“The dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.”
“Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that ye go to enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron?”
“If I be a man of God, then let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty.”
“Thus saith the LORD, Forasmuch as thou hast sent messengers to enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron, is it not because there is no God in Israel to enquire of his word?”
TO JEHORAM OF JUDAH, IN WRITING
“Behold, with a great plague will the LORD smite thy people, and thy children, and thy wives, and all thy goods”
The prophets of Baal at the Kishon
A cloud like a man's hand
Wind, earthquake, fire and a still small voice
Who stood with him, and against him

As he and Elisha “still went on, and talked”, a chariot of fire and horses of fire parted them, “and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven”. Elisha cried, “My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof”, and saw him no more. 2 Kings 2:11–12
Fifty strong men of the sons of the prophets searched for three days “but found him not”. 2 Kings 2:16–17
From the textKings records no death and no grave for Elijah. 2 Kings 2:11–18
Malachi closes: “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children”. Malachi 4:5–6
The angel told Zacharias that his son John would “go before him in the spirit and power of Elias, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children”. Luke 1:17
Asked “Art thou Elias?”, John answered, “I am not.” John 1:21

Jesus said of John, “if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come”; after the transfiguration, asked why the scribes say that Elias must first come, he answered, “Elias truly shall first come, and restore all things. But I say unto you, That Elias is come already, and they knew him not”, and “the disciples understood that he spake unto them of John the Baptist”. Mark has “Elias verily cometh first” and “Elias is indeed come”. Matthew 11:14 Matthew 17:10–13 Mark 9:11–13
On the mountain “there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him”; Luke adds that they “spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem”. Matthew 17:3 Mark 9:4 Luke 9:30–31
Some said Jesus was Elias; at the cross some heard him cry and said, “This man calleth for Elias”. Matthew 16:14 Mark 6:15 Luke 9:8 Matthew 27:47–49 Mark 15:35–36
When a Samaritan village would not receive Jesus, James and John asked whether they should command fire from heaven, in the KJV's words “even as Elias did”; he rebuked them. Luke 9:52–55

Ecclesiasticus, in the Apocrypha, praises Elias who “was taken up in a whirlwind of fire” and was “ordained for reproofs in their times ... to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob”. Sirach 48:1 Sirach 48:9–10 [9] Who says so: Jesus son of Sirach, Ecclesiasticus 48 (KJV Apocrypha), about 200 BC on T. W. Davies's dating; scholars differ

In Justin's Dialogue the Jewish speaker Trypho says, “we all expect ... that Elijah when he comes will anoint him”; Justin answers that Elijah will come before Christ's second coming, and that the Spirit of God who was in Elijah came as herald in John.[10] Who says so: Justin Martyr, Dialogue with Trypho 49, second century AD

Tertullian holds that Enoch and Elijah did not die but are “reserved for the suffering of death”, to die at the time of Antichrist.[11] Who says so: Tertullian, A Treatise on the Soul 50, early third century AD

Hippolytus names “the two prophets Enoch and Elias” as the two witnesses who will preach 1,260 days clothed in sackcloth before the end.[12] Who says so: Hippolytus, Treatise on Christ and Antichrist 43, early third century AD

Augustine calls it “a familiar theme in the conversation and heart of the faithful” that before the judgement the Jews will believe through Elias, who will come; “we have good reason to believe that he is now alive”.[13] Who says so: Augustine, The City of God 20.29, written between AD 413 and 426
Born at a Tishbe in Galilee, living in Gilead

Keil takes Tishbe as the town in Upper Galilee named in Tobit 1:2, Elijah's birthplace, and reads “of the settlers of Gilead” as meaning that he lived in Gilead away from his home tribe. 1 Kings 17:1 [1]
Tishbe was a place in Gilead
“Most modern commentators”, following the Greek Septuagint (F. K. Farr, ISBE 1915, p. 930); H. Ewald and O. Thenius (as reported, and rejected, by Keil, p. 235)

Farr writes that if the Septuagint reading is followed, as most modern commentators do, the Hebrew word read “inhabitants” or “sojourners” is itself “Tishbeh”, so that Tishbe lay in Gilead. Keil reports Thenius and Ewald for a Tishbe in Gilead and rejects it. 1 Kings 17:1 [8][1]

Kings does not name Elijah's father or tribe, and records no call.
Scripture does not say how old Elijah was, or in which year he was taken up; Kings records no death and no grave.
Kings does not say that Elijah anointed Hazael or Jehu; the anointing of Jehu is done by a young prophet Elisha sent.
Scripture does not say whether Elijah wrote anything besides the writing to Jehoram in 2 Chronicles 21:12.
The text does not say where Tishbe was; the site's map has no place for it.
